security_audit.summary: The Ruby shell execution alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code formatting in SKILL.md. The hardcoded Rube MCP URL is a confirmed low-risk external service dependency. The system reconnaissance alerts are false positives on Segment validation and PII guidance.

remediation.issue: External MCP endpoint handles Segment operations.
remediation.suggestion: Document Rube and Composio data handling, required auth scope, and approval expectations before users send customer data.

remediation.issue: Sensitive customer traits may be sent through workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation before sending email, name, IP address, user agent, or similar customer fields.

remediation.issue: Markdown tool names trigger command execution alerts.
remediation.suggestion: State that backticked names are MCP tools, not shell commands, to reduce static analyzer noise.

static_findings.snippet: - Active Segment connection via `RUBE_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS` with toolkit `segment`
- Always call `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` first to get current tool schemas
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
1. Verify Rube MCP is available by confirming `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` responds
- `timestamp`: ISO 8601 timestamp (optional; defaults to server time)
- `context`: Object with contextual metadata (IP, user agent, etc.)
- At least one of `userId` or `anonymousId` is required
- `event` name is required and should follow consistent naming conventions
- `traits`: Object with user properties (email, name, plan, etc.)
- At least one of `userId` or `anonymousId` is required
- To remove a trait, set it to `null`
1. `SEGMENT_BATCH` - Send multiple Segment calls in one request [Required]
- `batch`: Array of message objects, each with:
- Each message in the batch must have a valid `type` field
- `traits`: Object with group properties (name, industry, size, plan)
- `groupId` is required; it identifies the company or organization
- `properties`: Object with page-specific properties (url, title, referrer)
- At least one of `userId` or `anonymousId` is required
- `name` and `category` are optional but recommended for proper analytics
- `previousId` is the anonymous/old ID, `userId` is the new/identified ID
- Always include `userId` or `anonymousId` on every call
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
- Avoid sending PII in traits unless destinations are configured for it
- Each message in the batch must have a valid `type` field
- Avoid sending sensitive PII unless destinations are configured for it

content.user_title: Automate Segment Workflows with Rube MCP
content.value_statement: Segment operations can be slow when teams need repeated tracking, identity, group, page, alias, and batch calls. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured workflow for Rube MCP Segment tools.
actual_capabilities: Guides setup for Rube MCP and an active Segment connection.
Maps workflows for track, identify, group, page, alias, batch, and source tools.
Lists required fields for identifiers, event names, traits, groups, timestamps, and context.
Explains pitfalls for identity resolution, batch limits, schema consistency, and response parsing.
Recommends searching current Rube tool schemas before each Segment workflow.
limitations: Requires Rube MCP and an authenticated Segment connection.
Does not include executable code or direct API credentials.
Cannot verify current Segment schemas without live Rube MCP access.
May process sensitive customer data if users provide it to Segment tools.

use_cases.title: Validate event tracking
use_cases.description: Send consistent track and page calls during instrumentation checks.

use_cases.title: Update lifecycle profiles
use_cases.description: Prepare identify, group, and batch operations for onboarding or campaign segments.

use_cases.title: Review source configuration
use_cases.description: Inspect source schema settings and plan controlled Segment source changes.

prompt_templates.title: Track one event
prompt_templates.prompt: Use segment-automation to prepare one track event. Search current Rube tools first. Confirm the user identifier, event name, properties, and timestamp before sending.

prompt_templates.title: Identify a user
prompt_templates.prompt: Use segment-automation to identify a user. Search current schemas first. Prepare traits for [user]. Exclude sensitive PII unless I approve it.

prompt_templates.title: Batch lifecycle events
prompt_templates.prompt: Use segment-automation to batch these lifecycle events. Validate each message type and required field. Summarize errors or missing values before sending.

prompt_templates.title: Review source settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Use segment-automation to review source schema settings for [source ID]. Propose safe changes only. Wait for approval before any update.

output_examples.input: Track an Order Completed event for a known user.
output: The assistant searches the current Segment tool schema first.
It confirms the user identifier, event name, approved properties, and timestamp.
It asks for approval before sending the event through Rube MCP.

output_examples.input: Prepare a batch import for signup and onboarding events.
output: The assistant groups the requested messages by Segment call type.
It checks that every message has an identifier and required fields.
It reports missing values and waits before sending the batch.

output_examples.input: Review source schema settings before a configuration change.
output: The assistant searches source management tools and retrieves the current settings.
It summarizes the proposed change and possible collection impact.
It requires approval before updating the Segment source.

best_practices: Call RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS before selecting any Segment operation.
Confirm identifiers, timestamps, and event names before sending data.
Review PII handling and destination settings before adding traits or context fields.
anti_patterns: Sending sensitive PII without a destination and policy review.
Using alias repeatedly for the same identity merge.
Batching mixed messages without validating each required field.

faq.question: Does this skill send data by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance for MCP tools. Users still need active Rube and Segment access.

faq.question: Can it manage Segment identities?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers identify, alias, group, page, track, batch, and selected source operations.

faq.question: Does it include current Segment API schemas?
faq.answer: No. It instructs the assistant to search Rube tool schemas before use.

faq.question: Is PII safe to send?
faq.answer: Only send sensitive traits when your Segment destinations and policies allow it.

faq.question: Can it update Segment source settings?
faq.answer: Yes, but updates should be reviewed because source changes can affect data collection.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when Rube MCP is available.
